mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered quarters, or the average return is not significantly below the median baseline at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase of 0.4 percentage points or more over the prior month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by ≥0.4pp for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes, or the false-positive rate exceeds 50% in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more, coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) of less than 2%, signals a supply-side contraction with weak housing demand, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < 2%
regime_hint: manufacturing contraction with weak housing demand
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to produce negative 20-day returns in at least 55% of triggered months, or the predictive ROC is not statistically significant at 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% within a single month, in the context of a previous tightening cycle, signals a policy pivot toward accommodation that lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.75pp in one month after >2 consecutive months of increases
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes, or the hit ratio is below 50% in out-of-sample validation.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures growth (implied from GDPC1), both over two consecutive months, signals increased precautionary saving and weakening demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS up for 2 months AND GDPC1 growth slows (YoY change falls for 2 months)
failure_condition: The joint signal does not produce negative 60-day returns in at least 60% of triggered periods, or the median return is not statistically below the baseline at 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 for four consecutive months, with stable unemployment (UNRATE change within ±0.1pp), signals robust labor market expansion that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 50,000 for 4 consecutive months AND |UNRATE change| ≤ 0.1pp each month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes, or the hit ratio is below 50% in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) of more than 10% from its 12-month moving average, without a corresponding decline in industrial production (INDPRO), signals a housing-specific demand shock that disproportionately affects construction and related sectors, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 90% of 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months AND INDPRO not below 98% of 12-month MA
failure_condition: The joint signal does not produce negative 60-day returns in at least 55% of triggered quarters, or the predictive power is not robust to regime shifts.
